Hannah — thanks for sending this over and for the straightforward list. Below is a concise summary of Redwood's defaults and the controls you can use; I put the high-risk/PHI items first.

Short answers (high level):
- Default storage: Hosted API does NOT persist prompts/outputs to durable storage unless you opt into call logging ("enable_call_logging"). By default, requests are handled in-memory and transient caches are dropped after the response.
- Logging/retention: When call logging is enabled for an account, logs are stored in the customer's region and retained 30 days by default (configurable 0–365 days).
- KV cache/session state: Runtime KV cache is in-memory only; we do not write session-level KV to disk for hosted accounts. Dedicated/Private customers can opt into persistent session-store for long-running state, but that is explicit and documented in the Dedicated config.
- PII treatment: Fields marked as PII via the SDK flag or via our redaction rules are hashed using an account-scoped HMAC-SHA256 (deterministic) before being used in telemetry/duplicate detection; raw PII is not included in persisted debug logs.
- CMK/HSM: Customer-managed keys are supported for Dedicated and Private deployments; hosted customers can request a KMS-backed option for enterprise contracts (we can outline the steps).
- Audit & access: Audit logs for data access are available and retained according to the account retention window; role-based access + SSO protects access to stored logs.

More detail (useful bullets):
- Hosted default: no persistent prompt/output storage. Exceptions are explicit: (a) enable_call_logging = true, (b) snapshot_for_eval = true. Both are off by default.
- Retention tiers when logging enabled: Debug traces (full structured event traces) = default 7 days; Call logs (request/response payloads) = default 30 days; Aggregated metrics (latency, token counts) = 90 days. You can shorten/extend these per-account within 0–365 days for call logs.
- Residency: For US accounts we store logs in US regions; EU accounts in EU regions. Cross-region replication is off by default.
- Redaction: PII flagged by the SDK or our pattern-based redactor is replaced with deterministic HMAC tokens in persisted stores; we store the HMAC and token type but not the plaintext. For customers that need reversible pseudonymization for specific workflows, we offer a Dedicated/Private option with CMK and a documented access workflow.
- KV cache: short-lived, per-request; never checkpointed to disk in Hosted.

Next steps I propose:
1) I'll attach a 1-page summary you can hand to your procurement/security team.
2) Ben (cc'd) will open an evaluation account with logging off so your engineers can test without persistence.
3) If your SecOps wants a deeper write-up (redaction algorithm, sample logs with PII hashed), we can provide a redacted sample and a short tech note — will need an NDA or PoP depending on specific details.

I'll attach the summary in my next email. If any of these items need to be stricter (e.g., strict no-storage for certain endpoints), tell us the rule and we can document a config that enforces it.

Daniel — thanks, good questions. Below are firm confirmations and the operational steps we use for CareCompass accounts.

Confirmations:
- Persistent writes: Confirmed. Hosted requests are not written to durable object storage or DB by default — only kept in memory and dropped after processing. Persistent writes occur only when enable_call_logging OR snapshot_for_eval are explicitly enabled for an account.
- Example of persisted PII token: When a field is marked PII we emit and store a deterministic HMAC-SHA256 token (hex) using an account-scoped salt. Example (redacted): pii_email_hmac = "hmac:3f7a1e9b...". That token is non-reversible without the account salt and enables correlation across requests. We will provide a redacted sample log showing the HMAC format; no plaintext will be included.
- Deletion SLA: Programmatic deletion by account or by request ID is supported for logged artifacts. Standard SLA for deletion requests is 48 hours for accounts with logging enabled; emergency deletion (legal/incident) is 8 hours and we follow an agreed escalation chart. All deletions are audited.
- Sampling: Redwood does NOT sample request payloads for internal monitoring on hosted accounts by default. Sampling is only enabled for specific debug engagements and is disabled unless a customer consents. For enterprise contracts we can set sampling to 0% in the account config.
- Access: Only the Security and SRE teams have access to raw call logs for debug, and access is gated by time-limited tickets, MFA, and annotated audit logs. Product/Analytics teams only see aggregated metrics unless explicit approval is provided. We can provide a role/access matrix for procurement.

Operational steps for CareCompass PoC:
1) We will provision a PoC account with call logging disabled.
2) If you request log-enabled testing, we'll enable call logging on a per-environment basis (staging only) and set retention to 30 days or your requested TTL.
3) We'll provide a redacted sample log bundle (HMACs in place of PII) and a summary doc (attached).

I've attached a short 1-page response (olga-cc-response-20280712.pdf) that you can hand to procurement; Ben will follow up to create the evaluation account. If you'd like a signed statement for procurement (short ATO note) we can draft one for review.
